body:
Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 1 Foods that are Authorized I. Infant Formula (Category 21). a. Infant formula is defined in section 201(z) of the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act (FFDCA) (21 USC 321[z]) and meets the requirements in section 412 of the FFDCA 21 USC 350(a) and in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 21, Parts 106 and 107. b. WIC infant formula refers to iron-fortified infant formula which, other than water, does not require the addition of any ingredient. It is a complete food for an infant. c. Infant formula is not an equal substitute for human milk and breastfeeding. Breastfeeding must be maintained or increased, supported, and encouraged, unless medically contraindicated. d. Standard formulas. i. Powdered formula—most common, least expensive form of formula. ii. Concentrate formula. iii. Ready-to-feed formula. e. The amount of formula issued to a participant is based on many factors including the full nutrition benefit and monthly maximum allowances (MMA) outlined in Table 1 to paragraph (e)(9) in CFR Part 246, a breastfeeding assessment, and the WIC Formula and Food Authorization Form (FAFAF) if applicable. f. Primary contract formulas. i. Under the Child Nutrition Act of 1966, the infant formula manufacturers for WIC programs are selected via a competitive, sealed, bidding process. Competitive bidding is defined as a process under which the state selects a single source offering the lowest price. The infant formula company who offers the lowest net wholesale cost or the highest rebate per unit of infant formula is awarded the contract. The formula company selected acts as the state’s single source, providing all infant formula in the forms and types originally spelled out in the invitation for bids. ii. The Utah WIC program presently has a rebate agreement to provide the primary contract formulas Similac Advance (cow milk based) and Similac Soy Isomil (soy based). Additionally Utah WIC has a rebate agreement for select forms of: 1. Similac Sensitive 2. Similac Total Comfort

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 2

iii. All infants on the Utah WIC program who need a standard infant formula shall receive a contract formula, unless a non-contract formula is medically prescribed with a FAFAF. iv. Similac Advance is the standard primary contract formula for full- term babies on the Utah WIC program who are not breastfed.

g. Non-contract formulas include non-contract infant formula, exempt infant formula, and WIC-eligible nutritionals. i. Non-contract infant formulas include products designed for normal infant feeding. These products must contain at least 10 milligrams (mg) of iron per liter of formula at standard dilution. Standard dilution is 20 calories (kcals) per fluid ounce. 1. Enfamil AR, Earth’s Best Organic Sensitivity, and store brands (Perrigo) are examples of non-contract infant formulas. ii. If religious eating patterns warrant a non-contract infant formula (category 21), a FAFAF is not required. iii. Non-contract formulas include products whose manufacturers do not have cost-containment contracts with the Utah WIC program. iv. Non-contract formulas ordered by a Utah state-licensed prescriptive authority using a FAFAF are approved by the Utah WIC program if they meet the minimum requirements and specifications for WIC formula as outlined in Table 4 to paragraph (e)(12) – Minimum Requirements and Specifications for Supplemental Foods, 246.10 of the Food and Nutrition Service, USDA federal regulations, and are approved by the state office. 1. Non-contract infant formula approvals may be limited if there is a comparable contract formula for cost-containment purposes. 2. Non-contract formulas may not be approved if the Utah WIC program manager determines the Utah WIC food budget is in a deficit situation and does not have sufficient funds in the food budget to reimburse the cost of the non-contract formula. In these situations, the state nutrition coordinator, formula and food manager, or local CPA may consult with the state-licensed prescriptive authority to determine an alternative formula that can be supported by the Utah WIC food budget.

II. Exempt Infant Formula (Category 31).

a. Exempt infant formulas comply with and are defined in section 412(h) of the FFDCA (21 USC 350 a[h]) and regulations at 21 CFR Parts 106 and 107.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 3

b. Exempt infant formulas are formulas that are used instead of standard formulas to manage the medical conditions listed below: i. Allergies ii. Cancer iii. GERD iv. Weight-for-length/BMI < 5%ile (0-5 yrs) v. BMI < 18.5 (18+yrs) vi. Inborn errors of metabolism vii. Chronic Renal Failure viii. Feeding Difficulties ix. Malnutrition x. Prematurity xi. Other ICD 10 Medial Dx

c. Refer to the Product Guide for details regarding these formulas, as well as instructions on use, issuance, and ordering.

d. Metabolic formulas i. These formulas are used to manage inborn-errors of metabolism such as phenylketonuria. ii. Refer to the Product Guide for metabolic formulas, as well as instructions on use, issuance, and ordering.

e. Hydrolysate formulas i. Most hypoallergenic formulas are hydrolysate formulas. ii. Formulas such as Nutramigen, Pregestimil (Mead Johnson), Alimentum (Abbott), and store brand hypoallergenic formulas (Perrigo) are hypoallergenic formulas made for easy digestion and are less likely to cause allergic reactions than other types of formulas. iii. Refer to the Product Guide for hypoallergenic formulas, as well as instructions regarding use, issuance, and ordering.

f. Low-iron formulas i. Low-iron formula is not allowed in Food Packages I and II, but is allowed in Food Package III due to (but not limited to) the following: 1. USDA recognizes the medical condition hemolytic anemia, a disorder where the body breaks down red blood cells faster than they can be made. Hemolytic anemia necessitates the restriction of iron intake through the use of low-iron formula. a. Must be prescribed by a healthcare provider on a FAFAF. ii. Refer to the Product Guide for low-iron formulas, as well as instructions on use, issuance, and ordering.

III. WIC-Eligible Nutritionals (Category 41).

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 4

a. WIC-eligible nutritionals represent enteral products that are specifically formulated to provide nutritional support for individuals with a qualifying condition when the use of conventional foods is precluded, restricted, or inadequate. b. WIC-eligible nutritionals must serve the purpose of a food, meal, or diet (may be nutritionally complete or incomplete), and provide a source of calories and one or more nutrients. They must be designed for enteral digestion via oral or tube feeding.

c. Refer to the Product Guide for WIC-eligible nutritionals, as well as instructions on use, issuance, and ordering. d. WIC-eligible nutritionals may not be the following: i. Formulas or products used solely for the purpose of enhancing nutrient intake (e.g., vitamin supplements), managing body weight (e.g., weight control products), addressing picky eaters, or for conditions other than those accepted on a completed FAFAF. ii. Medicines or drugs. iii. Hyperalimentation feedings (nourishment administered through a vein). iv. Enzymes, herbs, or botanicals. v. Oral rehydration fluids or electrolyte solutions. vi. Flavoring or thickening agents (e.g., Thick-It, Simply Thick, gelmix). vii. Feeding utensils or devices designed to administer a WIC-eligible formula or nutritional (e.g., feeding tubes, bags, pumps). viii. Sports or breakfast drinks. ix. Formulas while under hospital care. x. Parenteral nutritional products.

IV. Manufacturers Allowed to Supply Formula to the WIC Program. a. Manufacturers supplying formula to the WIC program must be registered with the Secretary of Health and Human Services under the FFDCA (21 USC 301 et seq.). b. Imported (manufactured outside of the United States) category 21 and 31 infant formulas are not authorized on the WIC program unless a waiver is provided by the FDA to the USDA for WIC to authorize imported infant formulas under special circumstances such as a formula shortage, emergency declaration, or natural disaster. V. Providing Formula Instead of Complementary Foods. a. Food Package III allows for additional formula to be provided for an infant who is 6 to 11-months-old and medically unable to consume

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 5

complementary foods. To receive this, the healthcare provider must indicate this on the FAFAF. b. Up to the 4 to 5 month MMA of formula may be issued to these infants when prescribed by the healthcare provider on the FAFAF. c. The 4 to 5 month MMA of formula cannot be provided only because the participant prefers a higher amount of formula or because they do not want complementary foods. VI. Package Sizes of WIC-Authorized Foods.

a. WIC-authorized foods have required packaging sizes.

b. WIC will pay for authorized foods up to the amount issued to a participant’s account. i. If the package or container amount exceeds the total amount available on a participant’s account, WIC cannot pay for it and the participant cannot pay a partial amount (except in the instance of Cash Value Benefit [CVB] balances). ii. When buying fruits and vegetables, the participant can pay the difference in cost if the total for fruits and vegetables purchased exceeds the CVB balance available to the participant. iii. Participants should be educated to choose package sizes that add up to or come close to the balance on their WIC account. However, they may choose to purchase less than the amount issued to their WIC account.

VII. Eggs.

a. Allowed: i. White medium, large, and extra large eggs. ii. Brown or white cage free medium, large, and extra large eggs. iii. Must be the store brand or private label. Cage free is allowed in specific brands listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. iv. 1 dozen (12 count) packages.

b. Not allowed: i. Hard-boiled, deli, liquid, omega-3, low in saturated fat, cholesterol- reduced, free-range, pasture-raised, or any other specialty eggs.

c. Eggs are deducted from the participant’s account in 1 dozen increments.

VIII. Cereal.

a. Cereal refers to any combination of the allowed cereals, hot or cold, adult or infant, listed on the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 6

b. Adult cereal must have at least 28 mg of iron per 100 grams (g) of dry cereal.

c. At least 75% of all allowed cereals must be whole grain.

d. Allowed: i. Only brands specified in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. ii. Hot cereal - 9.8 ounce (oz.) to 36 oz. sizes. iii. Cold cereal - 12 oz. to 36 oz. sizes.

e. Not allowed: i. Cereals with more than 21.2 g of added sugars per 100 g of dry cereal (i.e. not more than 6 g of added sugar per dry ounce).

f. Cereals are deducted from the participant’s account in 0.1 oz. increments.

g. The following substitution in Food Package III can be made if determined as appropriate by the health care provider per medical documentation: i. 32 dry oz. of infant cereal may be substituted for 36 oz. of breakfast cereal. ii. A woman exclusively breastfeeding multiple infants may substitute 48 dry oz. of infant cereal for 54 oz. of breakfast cereal.

IX. Whole Wheat Bread/Whole Grain Bread/Other Whole Grains.

a. Whole Wheat Bread, Buns, and Rolls i. Whole wheat bread must meet the FDA standards of identity (21 CFR Part 136.180). ii. Must contain whole wheat flour or bromated whole wheat flour as the only flours listed in the ingredients list. iii. Allowed: 1. Only brands specified in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. 2. 16 or 24 oz. packages. iv. Not allowed: 1. White bread. v. Whole wheat bread, buns, and rolls are deducted from the participant’s account in 16 or 24 oz. increments.

b. Whole Grain Bread, Buns, and Rolls i. Whole grain bread must conform to FDA standards of identity (21 CFR Part 136.110). ii. Whole grain bread must contain at least 50% whole grains with the remaining grains being either enriched or whole grain. iii. Allowed:

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 7

1. Only brands specified in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. 2. 16 or 24 oz. packages. iv. Not allowed: 1. White bread is not allowed. v. Whole grain bread, buns, and rolls are deducted from the participant’s account in 16 to 24 oz. increments.

c. Other Whole Grains i. Other whole grains refers to tortillas, whole wheat macaroni products, brown rice, oats, quinoa and other whole grains that are listed on the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. ii. Other whole grains may not contain added fats, sugars, oils, sodium, or added flavors or seasonings. iii. Tortillas 1. Allowed: a. Corn tortillas made from ground masa flour. b. Only approved brands listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. c. 12 to 32 oz. size options. 2. Not allowed: a. White flour, hard shells, and wraps. 3. Tortillas are deducted from the participant’s account in 0.1 oz. increments. iv. Whole Wheat Macaroni (Pasta). 1. Whole wheat macaroni must meet the FDA standards of identity (21 CFR 139.138). 2. Whole wheat flour or whole durum wheat flour must be the only flours listed in the ingredient list. 3. Allowed: a. Any shape or size that otherwise meets the FDA standard of identity for whole wheat macaroni (pasta) products (e.g., rotini, penne). b. Only brands listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. c. 16 oz. packages. 4. Whole wheat macaroni (pasta) is deducted from the participant’s account in 16 oz. increments. v. Brown Rice 1. Allowed: a. Instant-, quick-, or regular-cooking. b. Only store brands or private labels. c. 14, 16, or 32 oz. packages. 2. Brown rice is deducted from the participant’s account in 14, 16, or 32 oz. increments. vi. Oats

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 8 1. Must be 100% whole grain. 2. Allowed: a. Rolled, old fashioned, or quick. b. Only brands listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. c. 12 to 32 oz. size options. 3. Not allowed: a. Individual serving packets. 4. Oatmeal is not considered a Whole Grain option. It is considered and allowed as a Cereal option. 5. Oats are deducted from the participant’s account in 1 oz. increments. vii. Quinoa 1. Allowed: a. Only brands listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. b. 12 to 32 oz. size options. 2. Quinoa is deducted from the participant’s account in 16 oz. increments. viii. English muffins 1. Must be 100% whole grain. 2. Allowed: a. only brands listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. b. 12 to 24 oz. size options. 3. English muffins are deducted from the participant’s account in 0.01 oz increments. ix. Pita bread 1. Must be 100% whole grain 2. Allowed: a. Only brands listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. b. 16.8 oz. size options. 3. Pita bread is deducted from the participant’s account in 0.1 oz increments. X. Juice. a. Juice must be 100% juice and contain at least 30 mg of vitamin C per 100 milliliter (ml) of reconstituted juice. b. Fruit juice must conform to the FDA standards of identity (21 CFR Part 146). c. Vegetable juice must conform to FDA standards of identity (21 CFR part 156). Vegetable juice may be regular or lower in sodium.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 9

d. Allowed: i. Any juice brands and flavors listed on the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. ii. 64 ounce containers, or various sized convenient multi-packs are allowed. 1. 64 oz. bottled juice is standard issuance for children 1 year and older and all women. a. For participants with any type of diabetes or medical condition requiring low calorie diets, proper education and instruction should be given to the participant on the nutrition of fruit juice and the potential benefits of vegetable juice for this population. 2. Convenience packs of juice cannot be issued because of participant preference. They may be issued to participants who are unhoused or lack refrigeration.

e. Not allowed: i. Juices with added sugar or sweeteners. ii. Refrigerated juices (except orange juice), cocktails, nectars, freshly squeezed, fruit drinks, fruit-flavored aids, sodas, or other beverages that are not 100% juice. iii. Unpasteurized juice. iv. Tomato juices with added sugar, fats, and oils.

f. 64 oz. bottled juice is deducted from the participant’s account in 1 bottle increments.

g. Convenience packs of juice are deducted from the participant’s account in 1 oz. increments.

XI. Cow’s Milk and Milk Alternatives.

a. Cow’s milk i. Cow’s milk must conform to the FDA standards of identity (21 CFR Part 131.110). ii. Milk must be pasteurized and contain 100 IU vitamin D and 500 IU vitamin A per 8 oz. 1. The vitamin A requirement doesn’t pertain to whole milk. iii. Allowed: 1. Fat contents: a. Whole-fat b. Reduced-fat (2%) c. Nonfat or low-fat (skim/1%) 2. Sizes:

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 10

a. Gallon b. Half gallon c. Quart 3. Only store brands or private labels for gallon and half gallon sizes. 4. Store brand or private label, or name brands for quarts sizes. iv. Not allowed: 1. Raw or unpasteurized milk. 2. Flavored or Skim Royale/Delight. 3. Half & half, flavored milk and drinks, sweetened condensed milk, organic milk, eggnog, or any other specialty milk beverages that have been highly fortified, engineered, or processed. 4. Cow’s milk for infants. v. Whole milk is the standard milk issuance for 1-year-old children. 1. In Food Packages III-IV, reduced-fat (2%) or skim/1% milk may be issued to 1-year-old children as prescribed on a FAFAF or for whom overweight or obesity is a concern as determined by the CPA based on individual nutrition assessment and if the healthcare provider doesn’t deny this per FAFAF. vi. Skim/1% milk is the standard milk issuance for children 2 years of age and older and women. 1. In Food Packages III - VII, reduced-fat (2%) milk is only authorized for participants with certain conditions, including but not limited to being classified as underweight, or maternal weight loss during pregnancy. The need for 2% milk must be based on an individual nutrition assessment. 2. In Food Package III, whole milk may be substituted for skim/1% milk for children 2 years of age and older, and women, only as determined appropriate by the healthcare provider per FAFAF. Whole milk can only be issued in Food Package III if the participant is also receiving a medical formula. vii. Cow’s milk is deducted from the participant’s account in 0.25 gallon increments.

b. Other allowable milks or milk alternatives include: i. Yogurt ii. Cheese iii. Lactose-free milk iv. Acidophilus cow’s milk v. Ultra-high temperature (UHT) milk vi. Evaporated milk vii. Nonfat dry (powdered) milk viii. Goat’s milk, dry or liquid (whole fat only)

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 11

ix. Buttermilk x. Plant-based milk alternatives (e.g., soy milk) xi. Tofu

c. Yogurt i. Yogurt must conform to the FDA standards of identity (21 CFR Part 131.200) ii. For children and women, yogurt may be substituted for milk at the rate of 32 oz. of yogurt per 1 quart of milk. 1. No more than 64 oz. of yogurt are authorized per participant. iii. Yogurt must be issued in 32 oz. increments per fat content subcategory (e.g., you cannot issue 16 oz. whole-fat yogurt and 16 oz. reduced and nonfat yogurt). iv. Allowed: 1. Plain or flavored. 2. Fat contents: a. Whole fat b. Reduced-fat (includes low-fat) c. Non fat 3. Only approved brands listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. 4. 32 oz. containers only. v. Not allowed: 1. Yogurts sold with accompanying mix-in ingredients such as granola, candy pieces, honey, nuts, and similar ingredients, drinkable yogurts, or whips. vi. Issuing “000 Yogurt - Whole and Reduced Fat” allows the participant to purchase whole-fat or reduced-fat yogurt. vii. Subcategory “001 Yogurt - Whole Fat (Do Not Issue)” allows only whole-fat yogurt and cannot be issued. viii. Issuing “002 Yogurt - Reduced and Nonfat” allows the participant to purchase reduced-fat or nonfat yogurt. ix. Whole and reduced fat yogurt is the standard yogurt issuance for 1- year-old children. 1. In Food Packages III - VII, nonfat yogurt may be issued to 1- year-old children as prescribed on a FAFAF or for whom overweight or obesity is a concern as determined by the CPA based on individual nutrition assessment and if the healthcare provider doesn’t deny this per FAFAF. x. Reduced and nonfat yogurt is the standard yogurt issuance for children 2 years of age and older, and women. 1. In Food Package III, whole-fat and reduced fat or reduced and nonfat yogurt may be issued to children 2 years of age and older, and women, when whole fat milk is prescribed on a FAFAF, along with a medical formula.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 12

xi. Yogurt is deducted from the participant’s account in 32 oz. increments.

d. Cheese i. Must be domestic cheese made from 100% pasteurized milk and meet the FDA standards of identity (21 CFR Part 133). ii. For children and women, cheese may be substituted for milk at the rate of 1 pound of cheese per 3 quarts of milk. 1. For children and women in Food Packages IV-VI, no more than 1 pound of cheese per 3 quarts of milk may be substituted. 2. For fully breastfeeding women in Food Package VII, no more than 2 pounds of cheese per 6 quarts of milk may be substituted. 3. For women fully breastfeeding multiples, no more than 3 pounds of cheese per 9 quarts of milk may be substituted. iii. Allowed: 1. Types: pasteurized processed American, brick, natural cheddar, colby, monterey jack, mozzarella, muenster, provolone, and swiss (i.e., any of the allowed cheeses listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide). 2. Cheeses that are labeled low, free, reduced, less or light in sodium, fat, or cholesterol. 3. Only store brands or private labels. 4. Block, sliced, shredded, string/stick, or cubes. 5. 8 to 16 oz., and 32 oz. packages. iv. Not allowed: 1. Imported cheese, cheese foods, and cheese spreads. v. Cheese is deducted from the participant’s account in 0.25 lb increments.

e. Lactose-free milk i. Lactose-free milk may be authorized for: 1. Women and children over 1 year of age. 2. Participants who report symptoms of lactose intolerance. 3. Participants who report a condition or symptom that could benefit from the use of lactose-free milk. ii. Allowed: 1. Whole-fat, reduced-fat (2%), or skim/1% as appropriate. 2. Store brand or private label, or other brands listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. 3. Quarts, half-gallons, and 3-quart containers. iii. Lactose-free milk is deducted from the participant’s account in 0.25 gallon increments.

f. Acidophilus cow’s milk

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 13

i. Acidophilus cow’s milk is fermented milk that contains less lactose than unfermented milk. ii. Must conform to the FDA standards for identity (21 CFR Part 131.111). iii. It is indicated for children over the age of 2 and adults who: 1. May have lactose intolerance, but are not allergic to cow’s milk protein. 2. Are on continuous antibiotic therapy. iv. The CPA must document the specific reason for use in the participant’s file. v. Acidophilus cow’s milk is deducted from the participant’s account in 0.25 gallon increments.

g. UHT milk i. UHT milk refers to whole, 2%, and 1%/skim shelf-stable milk that requires no refrigeration. Refrigerate after opening and follow label instructions for storage. ii. UTH may be beneficial for participants with: 1. A scarcity of refrigerated milk, 2. Poor refrigeration facilities in the home, or 3. Milk contamination emergency. iii. Allowed: 1. Brands listed in the “UHT milk - more information” food help. 2. Quarts. iv. UHT milk is deducted from the participant’s account in 0.25 gallon increments.

h. Evaporated milk i. Evaporated milk refers to whole, 2%, and 1%/skim canned cow’s milk product that has been concentrated by removing half of the water. ii. It must meet FDA standards of identity (21 CFR Part 131.130). iii. Allowed: 1. Store brand or private label, Nestle or PET brands. 2. 12 oz. cans. a. One 12 oz. can only reconstitutes to 24 oz. milk, but is equivalent to 0.25 gallons in VISION. iv. Evaporated milk is deducted from the participant’s account in 0.25 gallon increments.

i. Nonfat dry (powdered) milk i. Nonfat dry milk is the product obtained when only water is removed from pasteurized skim milk. It contains not more than 5% by weight of moisture, and not more than 5.5% by weight of milkfat unless otherwise indicated. ii. It must meet FDA standards of identity (21 CFR Part 131.127).

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 14

iii. Nonfat dry milk can be substituted at an equal reconstituted rate to fluid milk. iv. Allowed: 1. Store brand or private label, Village Farm, or Carnation brands. 2. 9.6 to 64 ounce packages allowed. a. One 9.6 oz. package is equivalent to 0.75 gallons. b. One 25.6 oz. package is equivalent to 2.00 gallons. c. One 32 oz. package is equivalent to 2.5 gallons. d. One 64 oz. package is equivalent to 5 gallons. v. Nonfat dry (powdered) milk is deducted from the participant’s account in 0.25 gallon increments.

j. Goat’s milk i. Goat’s milk refers to the fluid or dry form of goat’s milk. ii. Goat milk must contain 100 IU vitamin D and 500 IU vitamin A per cup. iii. Only whole goat’s milk is available in Utah, but it may not be sold at all vendor locations. iv. Allowed: 1. Drake Family Farms and Meyenberg brands. 2. Fluid goat’s milk—half gallon and quart containers. v. Goat’s milk is deducted from the participant’s account in 0.25 gallon increments.

k. Plant-based milk alternatives i. Plant-based milk alternatives are allowed if they meet the following nutrient levels per 8 oz., in accordance with FDA fortification guidelines: 276 mg calcium, 8 gm protein, 500 IU vitamin A, 100 IU vitamin D, 24 mg magnesium, 222 mg phosphorus, 349 mg potassium, 0.44 mg riboflavin, and 1.1 mcg vitamin B12. 1. Soy milk and non-soy plant-based milk alternatives are allowed. a. The CPA will determine and document the need for soy milk as a substitute for milk. i. This determination must be based on individual nutritional assessment, and consultation with the participant’s healthcare provider, as appropriate. ii. This substitution may be made for situations that include, but are not limited to, milk allergy, lactose intolerance, and vegan diets. iii. Allowed: 1. Only approved brands listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. 2. Half gallons and quarts.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 15

b. The CPA will determine and document the need for non-soy plant-based milk as a substitute for milk. i. This determination must be based on individual nutrition assessment, and consultation with the participant’s healthcare provider, as appropriate. ii. Non-soy plant-based milk is only appropriate when a participant has both a cow milk protein allergy and a soy protein allergy. iii. Allowed: 1. Ripple milk (pea based) and Silk Kids Oatmilk Blend (pea and oat based). 2. Half gallon (48 ounce and 59 ounce containers) and quarts (32 ounce containers and 8 ounce 4 packs). 2. Plant-based milk is deducted from the participant’s account in 0.25 gallon increments.

l. Buttermilk i. Allowed: 1. Whole-fat or skim/1% as issued appropriately. 2. Store brand or private label, Darigold, and Meadow Gold. 3. Half gallon or quart sizes ii. Buttermilk is deducted from the participant’s account in 0.25 gallon increments.

m. Tofu i. Must contain a minimum of 100 milligrams of calcium per 100 grams of tofu. ii. For children and women participants, 1 lb of tofu may be substituted for 1 quart of milk, up to 4 lbs of tofu per participant. iii. Allowed: 1. Only approved brands (regular and organic) listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. 2. 14 to 16 oz. packages of block tofu. iv. Not allowed: 1. Tofu with added fats, sugars, oils, or sodium. v. Tofu is deducted from the participant’s account in 1 lb increments (i.e., each 14 to 16 oz. package is deducted as 1 lb of tofu).

XII. Peanut Butter

a. Peanut butter refers to creamy or chunky, regular or reduced fat, and can be salted or unsalted.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 16

b. Peanut butter must meet the FDA standard of identity (21 CFR Part 164.150). It must contain at least 90% peanuts by weight and contain no other oils besides hydrogenated oils.

c. Allowed: i. Only approved brands listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. ii. 15 to 18 oz. containers.

d. Not allowed: i. Peanut butter with added jelly, honey, chocolate, marshmallow, or similar ingredients. ii. Peanut butter spreads.

e. Peanut butter is deducted from the participant’s account in 1 jar/bag increments (i.e., each 15 to 18 oz. container is deducted as 1 jar/bag).

XIII. Nut and Seed Butters

a. Nut and seed butters refer to creamy or chunky, regular or reduced fat, and can be salted or unsalted.

b. Nut and seed butters must have a comparative nutritive value to peanut butter (i.e., protein and iron).

c. Nut and seed butters are only allowed when the WIC participant or household member has a peanut allergy.

d. Allowed: i. Only approved brands listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. ii. 15 to 18 oz. containers.

e. Not Allowed: i. Nut and seed butters with added marshmallows, honey, jelly, chocolate, or similar ingredients.

XIV. Beans, Peas, and Lentils

a. Beans, peas, and lentils refers to any dry beans, peas, or lentils in dry- packaged or canned forms, without added vegetables, fruits, meat, sugars, fats, or oils.

b. Allowed:

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 17

i. Black, black-eyed peas, butter beans, cannellini, cranberry, fat-free refried, garbanzo (chickpeas), mayocoba, great northern, kidney, lentils, lima, navy, pink, pinto, red, split peas, and white beans. ii. Only store brands or private labels. iii. 15 to 16 oz. cans or 16 oz. dry packages.

c. Not allowed: i. Flavored, bean soup mix, mixed beans, chili, baked beans, yellow beans, beans with meat, canned green peas, snap beans, green beans, and wax beans. ii. Beans, peas, or lentils with added vegetables or fruits. iii. Beans—baked beans, immature legumes such as those used in canned green peas, green beans, snap beans, yellow beans or wax beans, or soups.

d. Beans, peas, and lentils are deducted from the participant’s account in jar/bag increments. i. Each 15 to 16 ounce can is deducted as 0.25 jar/bag. ii. Each 16 oz. bag is deducted as 1 jar/bag.

XV. Fruits and Vegetables

a. Fruits and vegetables refer to any fresh, frozen, or canned fruits and vegetables, including organic and fresh or jarred salsa without added sugar or oil. They must meet the FDA standards of identity: i. Fresh fruits (21 CFR Part 101.95). ii. Canned fruits (21 CFR Part 145). iii. Fresh vegetables (21 CFR 101.95). iv. Canned vegetables (21 CFR part 155). v. frozen vegetables (21 CFR part 158).

b. Allowed: i. Fresh fruits and vegetables—any variety of fresh whole, pre-cut, or packaged fruits and vegetables without added sugars, fats, or oil. ii. frozen fruits—any variety of frozen fruits without added sugars, fats, oils, or salt (i.e., sodium). iii. Canned fruits—juice or water-packed without added sugars, fats, oils, or salt. Fruit must be listed as the first ingredient. iv. frozen vegetables—any variety of frozen vegetables without added sugars, fats, or oils. 1. Vegetables must be listed as the first ingredient. 2. May be regular or lower in sodium. v. Frozen beans (immature or mature)—beans purchased with the CVB may contain added vegetables and fruits, but may not contain added sugars, fats, oils, or meat.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 18

vi. Canned vegetables—any variety without added sugars, fats, or oils. May be regular or low in sodium. vii. Fresh cut herbs, ginger root, taro root, garlic, and coconuts. viii. Yams, sweet potatoes, and white potatoes. ix. Mushrooms, even though they are scientifically classified as fungi and not fruits or vegetables.

c. Not allowed: i. Dried fruits or vegetables, packages with dips or dressings, salad bars, party trays, dried herbs and spices, salsa with sugar, and pouches. ii. Mixed vegetables with noodles, nuts or sauce packets, and decorative flowers and blossoms. iii. Dried herbs, spices, vanilla bean, gourds, and decorative/painted pumpkins.

d. Cash Value Benefit (CVB) Amounts. i. CVB amounts are adjusted annually for inflation. ii. CVB amounts are issued in the following amounts: 1. $26.00 for children ages 1 through 4 years. 2. $47.00 for pregnant, partially-breastfeeding women out-of- range, and postpartum women (up to 6 months postpartum). 3. $52.00 for fully breastfeeding women and part breastfeeding in-range women (up to 1 year postpartum). 4. $78.00 for women who are fully breastfeeding multiple infants. 5. $11.00 or $22.00 for infants 6 through 11 months (See “Tailoring Food Packages” P&P).

e. The CVB amount is deducted from the participant’s account in $0.01 increments and is not taxed. i. The difference can be paid for by the participant if the total for fruits and vegetables purchased is greater than the CVB balance available to the participant.

XVI. Fish

a. Fish refers to sardines, light tuna, N. Atlantic Scomber scombrus or Chub Pacific Scomber japonicas mackerel, and salmon.

b. Allowed: i. Packed in water or oil and include bones or skin. ii. Regular or lower in sodium content. iii. Flavored such as lemon, herbs, or broth. iv. Light tuna must be store brand or private label.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 19

v. Salmon, mackerel, and sardines must be the approved brands listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. vi. Sardines, light tuna, and N. Atlantic Scomber scombrus or Chub Pacific Scomber japonicas mackerel in 3.75 to 30 oz. cans. vii. Salmon in 5 to 30 oz. cans or 5 oz. pouches.

c. Fish is deducted from the participant’s account in 0.01 oz. increments.

XVII. Infant Foods

a. Infant foods refers to any regular or organic single or mixed infant fruits or vegetables, regular or organic infant meats, or infant cereal (non-organic).

b. Textures for all infant foods may range from strained to diced.

c. Infant Fruits or Vegetables i. A fruit or vegetable must be listed as the primary (first) ingredient in WIC-eligible jarred infant fruits or vegetables. ii. Allowed: 1. Organic. 2. Any single or mixed variety of commercial infant food fruits or vegetables (e.g., peas and carrots, apples and squash). 3. Brands as listed in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. 4. Infant fruits and vegetables that meet the minimum requirements and specifications for an infant food product and include white potatoes as an ingredient, but not the primary ingredient. 5. 2 oz. 2 packs, 4 oz. single jar, or 4 oz. multi-packs up to 128 oz. iii. Not allowed: 1. Mixtures with cereal and infant food desserts (e.g., peach cobbler). 2. Added DHA, sugars, salts, starches, or cereals. 3. Pouches.

d. Infant Meats i. Infant meat refers to any variety of commercial infant food meat or poultry as a single major ingredient with added broth or gravy, and without added sugars or salts. ii. Only exclusively-breastfed infants may receive infant meat. iii. Allowed: 1. Organic. 2. 2.5 oz. single jar or 2.5 oz. multi-pack up to 40 oz. iv. Not allowed: 1. Infant food combinations (e.g., meat and vegetables) and dinners (e.g., spaghetti and meatballs).

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Foods that are Authorized Page 20

2. Added DHA, sugars, salts, starches, or cereals. 3. Pouches.

e. Infant Cereal i. Minimum of 45 mg of iron per 100 g of dry cereal is required. ii. Allowed: 1. Any plain, dry infant cereal (i.e., corn, multigrain, oatmeal, or rice). 2. 8 oz. containers. iii. Not allowed: 1. Infant cereal with added infant formula, DHA, milk, fruit, or other non-cereal ingredients. 2. Pouches.

XVIII. Store Brand or Private Label.

a. Definition: A store brand (also called a private label) must be purchased when indicated in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide. i. Examples of store brands and private labels include but are not limited to: Food Club, Kroger, Great Value, WinCo, Signature Select, Lucerne, Freedom’s Choice, and Harmons. ii. If a store carries more than one store brand or private label, either store brand or private label may be purchased regardless of price.

b. For cost saving reasons, participants are required to purchase the store brand or private label of milk*, cheese, eggs, beans, peas, lentils, canned tuna, and brown rice. *Because store brand milk is not always available in quart size, specific brands of quart size milk are allowed.

c. When name brands are specified in the Utah WIC Program Shopping Guide, those brands may be purchased.

XIX. Other Products Not Authorized for WIC.

a. Foods with artificial sweeteners.

body:
Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Formula and Food Authorization Form Page 1

I. Utah Formula and Food Authorization Form (FAFAF).

a. FAFAFs are not required for the following Standard Primary Contract Infant formulas: i. Similac Advance ii. Similac Soy Isomil iii. Similac Sensitive iv. Similac Total Comfort

b. All other formulas and WIC-eligible nutritionals require a FAFAF for issuance.

c. FAFAFs are required for all children, at 12 months of age and older, who are receiving infant formula, including contract formula.

d. Medical order or prescriptive requirements to be filled out on the FAFAF. All of the following information must be included in order for the FAFAF to be considered complete and the product ordered or issued. i. Name of participant. ii. Participant’s date of birth. iii. Formula or nutritional prescribed. iv. Medical diagnosis warranting the issuance of the product. v. Form of product: Powder, Concentrate, or Ready-to-Feed (RTF). vi. Specific amount of formula prescribed (e.g., 3 cans per day). 1. A range is not appropriate. vii. Length of time the prescribed product is medically required. 1. A valid FAFAF may be written for up to 12 months, but no longer than 12 months. 2. Six months will be used as the default length of time, including the current month, if nothing is marked by the prescriber. viii. Signature and name of the requesting state licensed prescriptive authority or someone working under their supervision (i.e., physician [MD], doctor of osteopath [DO], nurse practitioner [NP], physician assistant [PA], certified nurse midwife [CNM]). ix. Clinic or hospital name, phone number, and fax number if applicable. x. Date FAFAF is completed. 1. A FAFAF is invalid if this date is older than 60 days from when it’s received in the WIC clinic.

e. Additional FAFAF requirements. i. The competent professional authority (CPA) must initial and date the completed FAFAF to indicate that it has met all of the above requirements. ii. A licensed prescriptive authority, or someone working under their supervision, is the only one allowed to complete a FAFAF. If it’s suspected that a participant completed the FAFAF themselves, the

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Formula and Food Authorization Form Page 2

CPA should call the participant’s healthcare provider to verify the information on the FAFAF. 1. If it’s determined the FAFAF was not completed by a prescriptive authority, a new FAFAF completed by a prescriptive authority must be obtained before the prescribed product can be issued. 2. If a new FAFAF completed by a prescriptive authority is not obtained, do not issue the prescribed product. 3. The CPA should discuss these situations with their clinic supervisor to determine if a participant violation is warranted. iii. Completed FAFAFs must be scanned into the participant’s record in VISION within 10 business days of when they’re received.

f. FAFAFs may be received as a hard copy, electronically, or as a facsimile (fax).

g. If a FAFAF is not available at the participant’s WIC visit: i. The CPA may receive the information prior to issuance by telephoning the prescriptive authority’s office. ii. The CPA must document all information obtained from the doctor or the doctor’s staff in VISION. This information must be read directly from the participant’s medical chart where any notes have been written by the prescriptive authority regarding the participant’s nutritional status or intake. iii. A completed FAFAF must be obtained within 2 weeks of the participant’s WIC visit. iv. Medical documentation received over the phone must only be used when absolutely necessary and on an individual basis. It should only be used to prevent undue hardship to a participant or to prevent a delay in the provision of formula that would place the participant at increased nutritional risk.

II. FAFAFs and Care Plans.

a. All children over the age of 12 months issued infant formula require a care plan when a FAFAF is received or renewed.

b. Care plans are required for high-risk participants whenever a FAFAF is received or renewed.

c. Participants who are not high risk do not require a care plan when a FAFAF is received or renewed (unless they’re a child over the age of 12 months issued infant formula).

d. If you receive a FAFAF with a medical diagnosis marked that’s not currently identified as a nutrition risk factor for the participant’s certification period, it must be added in a new risk record.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Formula and Food Authorization Form Page 3

i. If the newly assigned nutrition risk factor is designated as high risk, a care plan is required.

III. Out-of-State Prescriptions.

a. If a WIC participant transfers from another state and has a completed prescription on a WIC form from that state, the prescription may be honored for the time specified on the form. i. If the prescription is expired, the client needs to obtain a new FAFAF (Utah FAFAF or the form used by the state they previously received WIC in) before a non-contract formula or WIC-eligible nutritional is issued.

IV. Procedures Related to Formula Changes. If… Then. A healthy full-term infant shows symptoms of intolerance to the primary contract formulas… Refer them to their primary care provider. The participant must obtain a complete FAFAF if a non-contract formula is needed. A healthy full-term infant received a FAFAF for a non-contract formula because of symptoms of intolerance and the FAFAF has expired… Issue a primary contract formula. If a non- contract formula is still needed, refer the participant to their primary care provider for a new FAFAF. An infant or child is high risk and has been on a stated-ordered or non-contract formula and the parent/caretaker states the MD gave permission to transition to a primary contract formula. Their current FAFAF for the non-contract formula has not expired… Refer them to their primary care provider. Explain to the participant that the FAFAF must be honored for the time frame specified on the FAFAF. The participant or CPA must contact the primary care provider and obtain verbal or written approval for the primary contract formula before it can be issued. Documentation of this approval must be made in VISION. An infant or child is high risk and has been on a non-contract formula or nutritional. The parent/caretaker states the MD gave permission to transition to a primary contract formula or standard food package and the current FAFAF has expired… The CPA confirms with the parent/caregiver that the product is no longer needed and issues a contract formula or standard food package.

An infant or child is not high risk and the parent/caretaker states the MD gave permission to transition from a non-contract formula to a primary contract formula and their current FAFAF for the non-contract has not expired… The CPA must document in VISION that the parent/caretaker states the MD gave permission to transition to a primary contract formula. Issue primary contract formula. An infant or child is not high risk and the parent/caretaker states the MD gave permission to transition to a primary contract formula and their current FAFAF for the non-contract formula has expired… Issue primary contract formula.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Medicaid Reimbursement Page 1

Medicaid Reimbursement beyond Supplemental WIC

I. For WIC participants aged 1 years old and older who are receiving the WIC maximum amount of formula and enrolled in Medicaid or Medicaid Affordable/Accountable Care Organizations (ACOs), Medicaid may provide coverage for any additional formula above the WIC maximum under the conditions listed in the current Utah Medicaid Medical Supplies and Durable Medical Equipment Manual. Retrievable at: https://medicaid.utah.gov/utah- medicaid-official-publications/?p=Medicaid%20Provider%20Manuals/

Step Action 1 Notify the participant that Medicaid or Medicaid ACOs may provide any additional product. 2 Fill out the “Medicaid Fax – For Additional Formula” form on SharePoint. 3 Give the form to the participant to take to their health care provider who will assist in obtaining any additional formula that may be approved by Medicaid. 4 If the participant is receiving Traditional Medicaid, Healthy U, Select Health, Health Choice Utah or Molina Medicaid fax the “Medicaid Fax –IHC” form on SharePoint to the number printed on the form with the FAFAF.

II. Documenting Medicaid Provided or State Ordered Formula in VISION.

a. When a client is receiving a state ordered formula or formula that is being provided through Medicaid and receiving no other foods, this will need to be documented in the VISION system.

b. Documenting Medicaid-provided formula without issuing complementary foods: i. Select the “Special Diet” check box. Enter medical documentation information from the Formula and Food Authorization Form (FAFAF) under Documentation. ii. Select the appropriate “Medicaid-Provided Formula” or “State- Ordered Formula” model food package. iii. Select the “Direct Ship” check box in the food package grid. This allows the VISION system to recognize that the participant is receiving a state ordered formula benefit.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Medicaid Reimbursement Page 2

c. Documenting Medicaid-provided formula and issuing complementary foods: i. Select the “Special Diet” check box. Enter medical documentation information from the Formula and Food Authorization Form (FAFAF) under Documentation. ii. Select an appropriate model food package with the desired complementary foods. iii. Medicaid-provided formula does not need to be added to the food package grid because the system recognizes benefits are being issued.

body:
Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Ordering Formula from the State Page 1

Ordering Formula from the State

I. In situations where the individual is eligible for both WIC and Medicaid benefits, Medicaid is the primary payor. The formula is provided by a Medicaid-enrolled medical supply company, as long as the member meets policy criteria and the nutritional service is a covered benefit. In all other circumstances, WIC is the primary payor and provider.

a. Have the participant work directly with Medicaid and their healthcare provider if they have questions about meeting policy criteria and covered nutritional services.

b. WIC continues to be a supplemental program. See food package policy for maximum formula amounts provided by WIC and allowed by USDA policy.

c. A participant, caregiver, medical supply company, Medicaid, healthcare provider or someone working under their supervision can provide verbal confirmation that Medicaid denied coverage. This is acceptable to confirm that WIC is the primary payor and provider of formula.

II. State-ordered formula is meant to refer to any infant formula, exempt infant formula, or WIC-eligible nutritional that is unavailable or extremely difficult to find in stores and has been approved in the Product Guide to be a state-ordered formula. These products may also be referred to as “special formula.”

a. If a product is available through local vendors and the pharmacy, the product should be issued to the participant’s account to be purchased through the local vendor─not ordered as a special formula.

b. If a product has limited availability through local vendors and the participant has circumstantial hardship (e.g., transportation challenges, medical challenges), you must receive approval from a state registered dietitian (RD) before it can be ordered as special formula. i. Contact a state RD via phone or email. ii. Local staff must document state RD approval in the comments section of the special formula order form.

c. If a product is not available through local vendors, the product can be ordered as special formula.

III. The only staff authorized to order state-ordered formula are competent professional authorities (CPAs) who have successfully completed the special formula training (see ‘Staff Training’ policy; IV. Organization and Management/Staffing and Training Requirements/Staff Training).

IV. Issuing Only State-Ordered Formula in the Food Package Screen in VISION.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Ordering Formula from the State Page 2

a. Select the “Special Diet” check box. Enter medical documentation information from the Formula and Food Authorization Form (FAFAF) under ‘Documentation’.

b. Select the model food package from the drop-down list according to the participant’s category, breastfeeding description, and what category of formula or nutritional they are receiving (21, 31, or 41). i. Refer to the Product Guide to determine if the needed product is classified as a category 21, 31, or 41 product. The model food packages you can select from are: 1. “State Ordered Formula 0-5 mos” 2. “State Ordered Formula No Food” ii. If the participant is issued formula or a nutritional to purchase with their WIC card, and needs state-ordered formula as well, include both on their food package. 1. VISION recognizes state-ordered formula as a set number of ounces. If you are unable to verify the food package because VISION is calculating too many ounces are being issued to the participant, issue the product that the participant will purchase at the store and include a comment on their food package that they are receiving state-ordered formula as well. Include the category of the product(s). 2. If the participant is receiving more than 1 state-ordered product, and the products are different categories, select the category of the product they are receiving more of and include a comment on their food package that they are receiving multiple state-ordered products. Include the category of the product(s).

c. If an infant is partially breastfeeding out of range, and receiving state- ordered formula, select the “State Ordered Formula 0-5 mos” model food package and change the quantity from “1” to “2.” This will move the infant to the out-of-range amount and allow the mom to receive a postpartum food package if the infant is < 6 months old.

d. The “Direct Ship” box must be selected in the food package grid on the state-ordered formula line. This allows VISION to recognize that the participant is receiving a state-ordered formula and that it will not be available on their account.

e. Verify the food package and issue benefits to the participant. No benefits will be issued to the participant’s account because the “Direct Ship” box was checked, but this still must be done.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Ordering Formula from the State Page 3

V. Issuing State-Ordered Formula and Foods in the Food Package Screen in VISION.

a. Select the “Special Diet” box. Enter medical documentation information from the FAFAF under “Documentation”.

b. Select the model food package from the drop-down list according to the participant’s category, breastfeeding description, what category of formula or nutritional they are receiving (21, 31, or 41), and the participant’s food preferences or prescription. i. Add the desired 21, 31, or 41 state-ordered formula to the food package if it is not already included in the model food package you chose. ii. Refer to the Product Guide to determine if the needed product is classified as a category 21, 31, or 41 product. iii. If the participant is issued formula or a nutritional to purchase with their WIC card, and needs state-ordered formula as well, include both on their food package. 1. VISION recognizes state-ordered formula as a set number of ounces. If you are unable to verify the food package because VISION is calculating too many ounces are being issued to the participant, issue the product that the participant will purchase at the store and include a comment on their food package that they are receiving state-ordered formula as well. Include the category of the product(s). 2. If the participant is receiving more than one state-ordered product and the products are different categories, select the category of the product they are receiving more of and include a comment on their food package that they are receiving multiple state-ordered formula products. Include the category of the product(s).

c. The “Direct Ship” box must be selected in the food package grid on the state-ordered formula line. This allows VISION to recognize that the participant is receiving a state-ordered formula and that it will not be available on their account

d. Verify the food package and issue benefits. Only non-state-ordered formula benefits will be issued to the participant’s account because the “Direct Ship” box was checked.

VI. Ordering State-Ordered Formula.

a. The amount of product ordered as state-ordered formula (count) must be calculated based on the participant’s FAFAF and must not exceed the USDA maximum monthly allowance (MMA).

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Ordering Formula from the State Page 4

b. A state RD will review all state-ordered formula orders before they are submitted to the pharmacy. i. The state RD may need to consult with the local CPA before the final approval of the order. ii. If the local CPA left the “Count” field blank on the order form, the state RD shall determine and enter the count without consulting the local CPA.

c. Local staff must contact one of the state RDs if they have a question about the order they submitted or need to make changes to a submitted order.

VII. Receiving State-Ordered Formula in Local WIC Clinics.

a. Each clinic must keep a clinic receiving and issuance log. A clinic receiving and issuance log template can be found on SharePoint under the Nutrition tab. Clinics may also choose to create their own log that documents the same information.

b. Verify, and document in the clinic receiving and issuance log, that the following information is correct when the state-ordered formula is delivered to your clinic: i. Participant first and last name ii. Participant ID iii. Product name iv. Product count for issuance period v. Expiration dates on all packaging 1. Do not accept product that expires in less than 90 days of the date of delivery. vi. Condition of all packaging. 1. If product is open, damaged, or dented do not accept it.

c. Local WIC staff will sign or initial pharmacy records and the clinic receiving and issuance log to verify that the product delivered is correct based on the approved order and that it meets these standards.

d. The “Clinic Received Date” must be entered in the SharePoint order form after it is delivered and verified in the clinic. This will move the order form to “Clinic Received” status. i. Local staff must enter the date the product was delivered to their clinic where indicated on the SharePoint order form. ii. The pharmacy must update the status of the order to “Pharmacy Sent’” before clinic staff can enter the “Clinic Received Date.” Please allow 24 hours after delivery of the product for the status to be updated by the pharmacy. If the status has still not been updated after 24 hours, contact the state RDs.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Ordering Formula from the State Page 5

iii. Local WIC staff must not change the status of the SharePoint order form except to change it from “Pharmacy Sent” to “Clinic Received.”

VIII. Storage of State-Ordered Formula in Local WIC Clinics.

a. Local agencies should only store small quantities of state-ordered formula for a limited amount of time. i. Monthly orders should be done for each participant needing state- ordered formula. ii. Monthly pick-up appointments should be scheduled.

b. Storage is required that minimizes the danger of loss due to theft, infestation, fire, spoilage, or other causes.

c. Unopened liquids or powders should be kept at room temperature.

d. Storage area should be free of pests.

e. Formula should be stored in a locked cabinet or locked room with limited access to minimize the danger of loss or theft.

IX. Reporting Lost or Stolen Formula.

a. Call the state WIC office to report any loss or theft of formula.

b. Document this in the participant’s Comments/Alerts section in VISION.

X. Issuing State-Ordered Formula to Participants.

a. Upon issuing state-ordered formula, document the following: i. Date the formula was issued to the participant. ii. Signature or initials of WIC staff issuing formula to the participant. iii. Signature of the participant, parent/guardian, or proxy. iv. Product name. v. Product count. vi. Product expiration date. vii. Issuance period.

b. Proration and issuance period alterations will be done in the local WIC clinic when necessary. i. State-ordered formula may need to be prorated, or the issuance period altered, for many reasons (e.g., late pick-up of formula, new FAFAF prescription). The amount of formula issued to a participant shall not exceed the prescribed amount on their FAFAF or the USDA MMA.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Ordering Formula from the State Page 6

ii. Always include the day you issue the formula when calculating how many days you will issue the product for. iii. There are 2 methods that can be used: 1. Method 1 (proration): Proration is based on the number of days remaining in the issuance period if the issuance period is from the 1st day of the month to the last day of the month. 2. Method 2 (altered issuance period): Staff may choose to provide the entire month’s allowance and adjust the beginning issuance date for the next issuance period. The issuance end date of the current issuance period would change to be 30 or 31 days from the date the participant picked up their product (28 or 29 days in February). The next month’s issuance period will start the day after the new issuance period end date.

c. Proration or issuance period alteration must be documented in the clinic receiving and issuance log. Staff may document proration on paper formula logs, in VISION, using an electronic tracking form, or another documentation method that is used in the clinic.

d. It is allowed to issue the current issuance period (when it is a partial month) and the next issuance period at the same appointment only when: i. state-ordered formula is issued to the participant for the first time. ii. state-ordered formula is issued to the participant late into the current month’s issuance period and you use “Method 1 (proration).”

XI. Returning State-Ordered Formula.

a. State-ordered formula may be returned to the pharmacy only if the product meets all of the following criteria: i. It is no longer needed. ii. It has not left the clinic. iii. It will not expire in less than 90 days.

b. Refer to the “Formula and Food Returns” policy for information regarding state-ordered formula that was returned by the client or is no longer needed but does not meet the criteria to be returned to the pharmacy (IX. Food Benefit Accountability and Control/Reconciling Checks/Food and Formula Returns).

c. Submit return requests through the special formula return process in SharePoint. i. It is best practice to submit a return request as soon as it’s known that the product is no longer needed.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Ordering Formula from the State Page 7

ii. Staff should use the product’s original order to create a return request. iii. Staff must only return an amount of a product that is less than or equal to the count on the original order form. iv. If 2 products were ordered on 1 order form, and staff only need to return 1 of the products, the count must be entered as 0 on the formula that is not being returned in the return order form.

d. Do not submit a return request if there was an error in the pharmacy delivery (e.g., wrong product or flavor being delivered, damaged product). Email all state RDs regarding errors in pharmacy deliveries.

XII. Ordering State-Ordered Formula for Participants Not Currently Certified on the Utah WIC Program.

a. Under rare circumstances, formula may be ordered for a participant who is not currently certified on the WIC program. Approvals will be made on a case-by-case basis.

b. These conditions must be met before staff can submit the order on SharePoint: i. The participant must have a Person ID (PID). ii. The participant must have a scheduled appointment to certify or recertify on the program. iii. The clinic must verify the participant is an active Medicaid recipient. iv. The participant must have a completed FAFAF with a qualifying medical condition and formula.

c. Staff must document the above conditions have been met on the SharePoint order form and in VISION in the following places: i. SharePoint order form: Plan/Comments ii. VISION: Family Alerts

d. State-ordered formula (or other WIC benefits) must not be issued to the participant until they are active on the WIC program.

XIII. Home Deliveries of State-Ordered Formula.

a. Under rare circumstances, formula may be delivered to a participant’s home who is not able to pick up their formula from the local WIC clinic. i. State RD approval is required before the order is submitted in SharePoint in these circumstances. ii. Approvals will be made on a case-by-case basis.

b. These conditions must be met in order to be considered for approval:

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Ordering Formula from the State Page 8

i. Participant’s situation must demonstrate substantial hardship to travel to the WIC clinic (e.g., transportation challenges, medical challenges). ii. Clinic staff should first ask the participant if they have trusted support people or proxies that could pick up the formula on their behalf.

body:
Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Tailoring Food Packages Page 1

Tailoring Food Packages I. The goal of the food package tailoring guidelines is to make sure that all participants receive the Utah WIC food package that best meets their individual nutritional needs.

a. The tailoring guidelines allow CPAs to issue food packages that directly correspond to the nutrition counseling they give.

b. There are many model food packages available within each participant category. Take time to review them before you tailor a food package. i. In VISION, model food packages are found in the Model Food Package drop-down list in the Food Package screen.

II. Food package tailoring must follow state-approved policies and procedures and may occur at the following times: a. WIC appointments. b. Any time that a prescriptive authority (e.g., healthcare provider) documents the need for a change.

c. At the request of the participant. d. At the discretion of the CPA, when appropriate. i. Changes may include decreasing or eliminating food(s) that the participant is not consuming. III. Food package tailoring is only allowed for individuals, and not for groups of individuals. a. Individual tailoring for economic reasons (i.e., to save program costs) cannot be performed in local WIC clinics.

IV. Food packages are to be assigned and tailored only by CPAs.

a. Foods prescribed or restricted by a healthcare provider, as indicated on a Food and Formula Authorization Form (FAFAF), must be followed when you assign or tailor a food package.

V. Changing food packages.

a. Non-formula food packages may only be changed in the current month if family benefits have not been purchased for the current month. i. When any family benefits have been purchased in the current month, the new food package with changes must start the following month.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Tailoring Food Packages Page 2

b. Formula food packages may be changed in the current month when there are changes to formula, even if family benefits have been purchased. Types of foods cannot be changed in the food package for the current month (e.g., you cannot change from regular cow’s milk to lactose-free milk). i. CPAs must check the “To Be Issued” amounts on the Economic Unit Balance-to-Issue pop-up window before benefits are issued. If any of the benefits to be issued are incorrect, the CPA must contact the Help Desk to correct the benefit amounts.

VI. The maximum monthly allowances (MMA) or full nutritional benefit (FNB) of all formulas and WIC-eligible nutritionals must be made available to participants.

a. Following a WIC nutrition and breastfeeding assessment of the needs of the dyad, breastfed infants, even those in the fully formula fed category, should be issued the quantity of formula needed to support any level of breastfeeding up to the FNB. This amount may be less than the FNB. b. Formulas and WIC-eligible nutritionals issued in VISION do not need to be prorated based on the date the food package is issued.

c. State-ordered formula must be prorated based on the date it is issued.

VII. The full quantities of all foods in each food package must be made available to participants.

a. The WIC food packages should not be tailored at the expense of the participant’s nutritional status.

b. Issuing less than the full quantity of all foods in a food packages is only appropriate when: i. Medically or nutritionally warranted (e.g., to eliminate a food due to a food allergy). ii. A participant requests to remove or decrease the quantity of food(s). 1. Reassure the participant that if their needs change, the food package can be increased up to the full quantity of foods again.

VIII. Documentation in VISION is needed when you tailor the food package in certain situations.

a. Documentation is required when you issue the following: i. Plant-based milk ii. Lactose-free milk

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Tailoring Food Packages Page 3

iii. Goat milk for 1-year-olds iv. Reduced and Nonfat subcategory of yogurt for 1-year-olds v. 2% milk for any participant vi. Nut and seed butters vii. CVB for infants 6 to 11 months old viii. Contract formula in ready-to-feed (RTF) or concentrate form ix. Foods or formulas as prescribed on FAFAFs

b. Documentation is not required when you issue the following: i. Legumes instead of eggs ii. Tofu at the allowed substitute rate for milk iii. More CVB instead of juice iv. Yogurt at the allowed substitute rate for milk v. Cheese at the allowed substitute rate for milk vi. Any other tailoring that is not listed above in VIII.a.

c. Documentation must be done in the “Comments” field below the food package grid in the Food Package screen. FAFAF item documentation only requires the “Documentation” screen on the Food Package panel be completed and the FAFAF uploaded to VISION within 10 days.

d. It may also be helpful to document reason(s) for tailoring in the participant’s care plan.

IX. Tailoring milk and milk alternatives.

a. Whole milk and whole and reduced-fat yogurt are the standard issuance for 1-year-old participants. i. Fat-reduced milks (i.e., 2% or skim/1% milk) and reduced and nonfat yogurt may be issued by CPA discretion to 1-year-old participants with certain conditions (i.e., Nutrition Risk Factors overweight or obese). 1. The CPA must document the medical or nutritional reason for issuance.

b. Skim/1% milk and reduced and nonfat yogurt are the standard issuance for children 2 through 4-years-old and women participants. i. Reduced-fat (2%) milk is authorized for participants with certain conditions (e.g., Nutrition Risk Factors underweight, low maternal weight gain). 1. The CPA must document the medical or nutritional reason for issuance. a. Transitioning between milk fat contents (e.g., whole milk to skim/1%), tolerance, increased milk intake, and preference are not allowable reasons for issuing 2% milk.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Tailoring Food Packages Page 4

ii. Whole-fat milk and whole-fat yogurt may be issued to children 2 through 4-years-old and women if they have a FAFAF for an exempt formula or WIC-eligible nutritional, and whole milk is prescribed on the FAFAF as well. 1. The participant may choose which fat content of yogurt they’d like in these situations. They may choose whole and reduced fat yogurt, or reduced and nonfat yogurt.

c. Milk alternatives may be used when tailoring the milk portion of food packages. i. Milk alternatives include: Cheese, yogurt, tofu, lactose-free milks, acidophilus milk, UHT, nonfat dry (powdered) milk, evaporated milk, goat’s milk, buttermilk, and plant-based beverages (i.e., soy milk or non-soy plant-based milk). ii. Lactose-free, soy, non-soy plant-based, and goat milks can be substituted for milk at a rate of 1 gallon to 1 gallon. iii. Cheese can be substituted for milk at a rate of 1 pound (lb.) of cheese per 3 quarts (0.75 gallon [gal.]) of milk without a FAFAF. 1. Maximum substitution amounts are as follows: a. 1 lb. of cheese (0.75 gal. of milk) for Food Packages IV-VI. b. 2 lb. of cheese (1.5 gal. of milk) for Food Package VII. c. 3 lb. of cheese (2.25 gal. of milk) for women fully breastfeeding multiples. iv. Yogurt may be substituted at a rate of 32 ounces (oz.) of yogurt for 1 quart (0.25 gal.) of milk. Yogurt may only be issued in 32 oz. increments. 1. Maximum substitution amounts are as follows: a. 64 oz. of yogurt (0.5 gal. of milk) for Food Packages III-VII. b. 96 oz. of yogurt (0.75 gal. of milk) for women fully breastfeeding multiples. v. Tofu may be substituted at a rate of 1 lb. of tofu for 1 quart (0.25 gal.) of milk without a FAFAF. 1. Maximum substitution amount is as follows: a. 4 lbs. of tofu (1 gal. of milk) for Food Packages III-VII and women fully breastfeeding multiples.

X. Tailoring legumes.

a. Legumes may be substituted at a rate of 1 jar/bag of legumes for 1 dozen eggs.

b. All eggs may be substituted for legumes in Food Packages III-VII and for women fully breastfeeding multiples.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Tailoring Food Packages Page 5

c. When a WIC participant or household member has a peanut allergy, nut and seed butters may be substituted at a rate of 1 jar/bag of nut and seed butters for 1 jar/bag of legumes.

XI. Tailoring juice.

a. The cash-value benefit (CVB) may be substituted for the juice benefit. i. Substitution amount is as follows: 1. $3 CVB for the entire juice benefit for Food Packages III-VII. 2. $4.50 CVB for the entire juice benefit for women fully breastfeeding multiples. 3. CVB substituted for juice may be substituted for jarred infant fruits and vegetables when prescribed on a FAFAF.

b. Convenience packs of juice are only allowed when there is a lack of refrigeration. i. Personal preference for convenient packs is not a valid reason for tailoring.

XII. Tailoring for special needs (e.g., participants experiencing homelessness, storage or refrigeration problems, or limited resources).

a. WIC participants who don’t have a permanent place of residence (e.g., due to loss of income, disaster, eviction, domestic violence situations) may be temporarily relocated to emergency shelters, motels, hotels, or makeshift abodes within their WIC service area. Due to this, access to cooking facilities, refrigeration, and acceptable storage areas for food may not be available. The types of WIC foods issued must take into account the cooking and storage facilities available to these participants. i. The “No Refrigeration” Food Package is meant to help accommodate participants in these situations. b. The CPA should determine the availability of the following before the food package is issued: i. Refrigeration for foods and prepared formula. ii. Cooking facilities. iii. Food storage facilities. iv. Eating utensils. v. The number and size of bottles for infant formula. vi. Bottle washing or sterilization capabilities. vii. The parent or guardians’ competence in preparation, storage, and feeding of WIC foods (especially foods that are perishable).

c. Specific education on the use and storage of foods should be provided.

XIII. Tailoring Food Packages II and III.

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Tailoring Food Packages Page 6

a. Food Packages II and III for infants 6 through 11 months. i. Infants, 6 through 11 months, may substitute: 1. Half of their infant food fruits and vegetables for $11.00 CVB and 64 oz. of infant food fruits and vegetables, or 2. All of their infant fruits and vegetables for $22.00 CVB. ii. This substitution may be made only after a CPA has assessed developmental readiness, safe food preparation, storage techniques, and feeding practices to make sure participants are meeting their nutritional needs in a safe and effective manner. iii. This substitution must be the choice of the parent or guardian and documented in the “Comments” field below the food package grid in the Food Package screen.

b. Food Package III for children and women. i. Qualifying medical conditions (e.g., prematurity, developmental delays, dysphasia [swallowing disorders]) may necessitate a medical order for jarred infant food fruits and vegetables or infant cereal. ii. CPA discretion alone to issue jarred infant food fruits and vegetables or infant cereal is not allowed. iii. The CVB may be substituted for jarred infant food fruits and vegetables if the participant has a FAFAF for an exempt formula or WIC-eligible nutritional, and pureed fruits and vegetables is prescribed on the FAFAF as well. 1. The quantity of jarred infant food fruits and vegetables issued is based on the substitution of 6.25 oz. of infant fruit and vegetables for $1 CVB, rounded down to the nearest whole 4 oz. jar. 2. If the CVB is substituted for jarred infant food fruits and vegetables, the full CVB amount must be substituted (i.e., you cannot issue half the CVB amount, and half jarred infant food fruits and vegetables). 3. If CVB is substituted for the juice benefit, that CVB may be substituted for jarred infant fruits and vegetables when prescribed on a FAFAF. iv. Adult cereals may be substituted for infant cereals if the participant has a FAFAF for an exempt formula or WIC-eligible nutritional, and infant cereal is prescribed on the FAFAF as well. 1. 32 dry oz. of infant cereal may be substituted for 36 oz. of adult cereal for women and children. 2. 48 dry oz. of infant cereal may be substituted for 54 oz. of adult cereal for women fully breastfeeding multiples. 3. If adult cereals are substituted for infant cereals, the full amount must be substituted (i.e., you cannot issue half infant cereal, and half adult cereal).

Utah WIC Local Agency Policy and Procedures Manual

II. Nutrition Services-Breastfeeding/Food Package Prescriptions/Tailoring Food Packages Page 7

v. The prescribed foods may still be issued, even if Medicaid is the primary payor of the prescribed exempt formula or WIC-eligible nutritional.
